title: Product discovery and validation
outcome: Test whether a product idea is worth building: shape the vision, understand the people and their journey, and plan the experiments that will prove or disprove it.

minimumInputs.help: What do you know about your users, and where does it come from?
minimumInputs.example: Six supplier interviews and the support inbox.

minimumInputs.help: What outcomes do you want for users and the business?
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers stop chasing; AP spends less time on calls.

minimumInputs.help: What limits apply (time, budget, technology, rules)?
minimumInputs.example: Must reuse our supplier login; launch within a quarter.

minimumInputs.prompt: Idea or need in the user's words
minimumInputs.help: Describe the idea or the need the way you would explain it to a friend.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers keep chasing us by email because they cannot see if their invoice was approved.

minimumInputs.help: What is in and out of scope for this exploration? Rough boundaries are fine.
minimumInputs.example: Invoice status only; payments and contracts are out of scope for now.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Anything not yet known about users, value or metrics is written as a hypothesis to test.

minimumInputs.prompt: Target group and attributed evidence or explicitly labelled hypotheses
minimumInputs.help: Who is the persona for, and what do you know about them? Mark guesses as guesses.
minimumInputs.example: Small suppliers (from interviews); we guess they mostly use phones.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. The persona will not invent ages, statistics or research you have not given.
Whose journey is this? Name the user or group.
minimumInputs.example: A small supplier submitting their first invoice.

minimumInputs.help: What are they trying to get done, start to finish?
minimumInputs.example: Get an invoice paid without having to chase anyone.

minimumInputs.prompt: Known touchpoints or explicitly hypothetical flow
minimumInputs.help: Which steps or contact points do you know about? If unsure, describe how you think it works and say it is a guess.
minimumInputs.example: Email invoice, wait, chase by phone, receive payment (we think).

minimumInputs.help: What do you believe is true but have not proven? Write it as a guess you can test.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers who can see invoice status will stop emailing accounts payable.

minimumInputs.help: How could you test that guess quickly and cheaply? Or describe a test you already ran.
minimumInputs.example: Email ten suppliers a status link for two weeks and count follow-up emails.

minimumInputs.prompt: Distinguish planned work from observed results
minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Planned steps and real results are kept apart, so nothing is reported as done before it happened.
What result do you want this work to deliver?
minimumInputs.example: Invoices approved within five days and fewer supplier complaints.

minimumInputs.prompt: User needs/opportunities with evidence or explicit hypotheses
minimumInputs.help: What do users need, and how do you know? Mark guesses as guesses.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers need to know payment dates (from support emails).

minimumInputs.help: What solutions could meet those needs, and what would you test first?
minimumInputs.example: Status portal or weekly email; test which reduces chasing.

minimumInputs.help: What question should the prototype answer?
minimumInputs.example: Can a manager approve an invoice on a phone without help?

minimumInputs.help: Who will try the prototype, and in what situation?
minimumInputs.example: A manager approving three invoices between meetings.

minimumInputs.help: What will the prototype include, and what will it fake or leave out?
minimumInputs.example: Clickable approval screens only; no real data or login.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Findings are only recorded from real test sessions, never assumed.
What problem are you solving, and for whom?
minimumInputs.example: Managers miss approval deadlines because invoices arrive by email and get buried.

minimumInputs.help: Who is the main user of what will be built?
minimumInputs.example: Approving managers who receive invoices for sign-off.

minimumInputs.help: What will be different when this is solved?
minimumInputs.example: Invoices approved in five days and early-payment discounts captured.

minimumInputs.help: What do you propose to include in this product version?
minimumInputs.example: Invoice capture, approval routing by amount, and posting to finance.

minimumInputs.help: What research or evidence do you have, and what limits apply? Say "none yet" if so.
minimumInputs.example: Interviews with six managers; must integrate with the current finance system.
